title: Editions within minutes, not hours: a dispatch-only token, or accept GitHub's schedule
note: Dev, 27 October 2026. Editions build in CI (board dev-0005), but GitHub fires the six's schedules (every ten and fifteen minutes as written) only about every four hours (16:48 and 21:00 on 27 October). So a change to the press is built at once and taken on the next push to each repository, but a change in data, team, site or updates waits for the next scheduled edition: hours. Live-drawn articles, records and briefs are on their pages at once either way. The fix needs one thing only you can make: a fine-grained personal access token (or a GitHub App) with Actions: read and write on the six repositories and nothing else, stored as a secret in each (EDITION_DISPATCH). With it, each repository's deploy starts the press's edition build after its release, and the edition's publish starts the six deploys: a release on its pages in about five to eight minutes. It can start workflows; it cannot push, read secrets or change code; every write stays with each repository's own GITHUB_TOKEN. Without it, nothing is wrong, only slower. A tokenless heartbeat (a workflow that re-dispatches itself every few minutes) would work too, but keeps runners busy around the clock, which GitHub's terms may treat as abuse; dev does not recommend it.
